name: renewal-dispatch
description: Flow 7. The T-90 per-entity timer (contract artefact 5 concern "renewal-dispatch", name renewal-dispatch:<policyId>). A wake-up, not a decision. It finds the renewal flow 6 wrote — by folder = <policyId> AND origin = publisher-renewal, never by the reference string, so a regeneration is picked up automatically — takes the newest one, reads its decision, and dispatches ONLY a clean undispatched ACCEPT on an ACTIVE, auto-renewal-eligible policy with no MTA open (spec 4.6.3: an MTA in progress marks the renewal Pending Expiring Endorsement and queues it for manual review). It renders tpl_quotation_schedule, writes the reference onto the renewal decision's issued_document_refs, and only then emails the Renewal Invitation — record first, notice second, as plan 5.3 rule 3 requires. Idempotency needs no new schema field: a non-empty issued_document_refs on the renewal decision IS the dispatch record. Timer payload: {policy_id, concern, quote_id}.

static.note_attachment: send-templated-email's contract is {to, to_name?, subject, body_html, email_class, idempotency_key?} — it carries no attachments, so the invitation names the rendered Quotation Schedule by object key rather than attaching it. Attaching it needs either an attachments field on that sub-flow or a broker-facing document fetch.
static.note_class: email_class transactional: a renewal invitation on an existing contract is a servicing notice to the broker of record, not an opt-out-bearing marketing send. Confirm with Antipodean before the first live broker.
